title: Financial Management AI
summary: An intelligent financial analysis and knowledge-augmentation system for personal investment research.
content: Combines market data, financial indicators, news and filings, and a personal investment knowledge base. Multi-model agents, OCR, and vector retrieval produce traceable structured analysis, risk signals, and research support.
capabilities: Multi-source market-data ingestion, cleaning, and scheduled synchronization
OCR knowledge-base processing, semantic retrieval, and vector storage
AI agent tool calls and structured investment-analysis reports

children.detail: Vue 3 administration, market dashboards, knowledge bases, and AI analysis views

documents.title: Financial Analysis AI · System Overview
documents.summary: A personal investment research system composed of a Java business core, Python intelligence workflows, and a Vue research workbench.

blocks.code:
Vue 3 Workbench
   ↕ WebSocket / REST
Spring Boot Core ── RabbitMQ ── Python AI Workers
   ↕ PostgreSQL / InfluxDB        ↕ pgvector / MinIO

items: Spring Boot owns authorization, assets, research entities, market snapshots, task state, and the internal data gateway.
Python owns LangGraph agents, OCR, embeddings, scene detection, and retrieval reranking.
RabbitMQ decouples long jobs; PostgreSQL/pgvector, InfluxDB, and MinIO hold structured, time-series, and object data.
Every conclusion remains tied to evidence records and time context.
Models read data only through authorized tools and never connect directly to business storage.
Async flows expose budgets, retries, dead letters, human review, and stage artifacts for recovery and audit.

documents.title: AI Chat Agent Architecture
documents.summary: Java protects identity, session, and data-access boundaries while Python LangGraph runs a budgeted, recoverable agent loop.

items: finance-app owns bootstrap and assembly; finance-ai orchestrates sessions over finance-service, finance-security, and finance-data.
Java owns authentication, WebSocket sessions, RabbitMQ delivery, and the internal data gateway; Python never queries the business database directly.
Python tool callbacks are HMAC-signed, and the signing secret never enters model context.

blocks.code:
context_gate → load_profile? → load_memory? → planner
             → tools → final_decision → final_stream

items: Graph State carries messages, profile, memory, scratchpad, pending tools, evidence records, and tool cache.
Only final_stream can emit answer_delta, keeping tool protocol separate from user-visible text.
Default budget: 6 steps, 10 total tool calls, 4 per step, 50-second timeout, and 2 final backtracks.

blocks.text: The agent may choose how to analyze, but it cannot bypass Java identity, authorization, or data contracts.

documents.title: finance-ai Module Architecture
documents.summary: The orchestration module combines chat, agents, OCR, knowledge, and reports while finance-service retains market and business-data ownership.

items: finance-ai is assembled by finance-app and exposes /api/ai/**, /api/knowledge/**, /internal/agent/**, and WebSocket behavior.
Controllers and services own AI use cases, converters stabilize DTO/VO/Map shapes, messaging isolates RabbitMQ, and providers assemble scene data.
Market, fundamental, and valuation reads remain in finance-service; the AI module reaches them only through business services and the internal gateway.

blocks.code:
Chat: Controller → Query Rewrite → Market Context → ChatClient
Agent: WebSocket → Session → RabbitMQ → Python → Callback
OCR/Report: Task → Stage Messages → Artifact / Result

items: Query Rewrite resolves domain, target, time range, and executable dataRequests before the answer model runs.
agent_progress, answer_delta, and final_answer are separate; only the final answer is persisted with token usage.
OCR, manual knowledge, and reports share task boundaries with stages, human review, re-embedding, and regeneration.

documents.title: Agent Tool Calling RAG
documents.summary: Controlled tools compute structured market scenes first, then derive a tagged knowledge query for compact evidence retrieval.

blocks.code:
question → scene_signal_context → scene processors
→ queryText + scenes + tags → knowledge_search → compact chunks

items: scene.signal_data reuses the Java SceneTargetDataProvider without creating a report task or publishing report messages.
Python expands seven-scene dependencies topologically; risk_strategy precomputes trend, valuation, and sentiment while returning only requested scenes.
Java validates session, scenes, tags, and limit before reranking knowledge by semantic, same-scene, and cross-scene signals.
Full candles, valuation history, and calculation parameters remain internal to processors.
Knowledge results are reduced to filename and content rather than exposing vectors or internal metadata.
Ordinary conversation skips RAG, and empty retrieval is represented honestly as insufficient evidence.

documents.title: Domain Tool Calling
documents.summary: Tools are divided by business meaning across quotes, stock fundamentals, convertible bonds, and prior reports to avoid duplicate fields and unbounded context.

items: market_quote owns current price, change, turnover, volume ratio, and current valuation snapshots.
stock_fundamental_context owns valuation history, financial indicators, and dividends; convertible_bond_context owns terms, premium, bond floor, YTM, and remaining size.
scene_report_context reads only reports visible to the current user.

blocks.code:
Python Tool → signed Agent Gateway HTTP
→ Java ActionHandler → Manage / Mapper
→ compressed domain response → tool evidence

items: Java caps sections and limits; a missing partition marks dataCompleteness.missing without discarding valid partitions.
Models select business tools instead of addressing storage tables.
The bounded agent loop still controls the total tool budget after new tools are added.

documents.title: OCR Knowledge Pipeline
documents.summary: A recoverable async pipeline turns images and PDFs into reviewed, categorized, and vector-searchable research knowledge.

blocks.code:
normalize → recognize → text.clean → quality.validate
          → rule_tag → llm_tag? → correct → embedding.index

items: Images use Qwen-VL OCR; PDFs use OpenDataLoader, with artifacts from every stage stored in MinIO.
Java creates tasks, manages human review, and confirms reviewed.json; generic Python workers consume RabbitMQ stage messages.
Normal, retry, and DLX exchanges separate the happy path, 30-second TTL retries, and dead letters.
Seven scene groups cover asset, price, volume, trend, valuation, sentiment, and risk strategy.
The rules-only path requires at least 2 nonempty categories and a maximum confidence of 0.75 or higher in each hit category.
Only weak results reach the LLM; correct merges, deduplicates, fills categories, and prevents empty documents from entering the vector index.

blocks.text: Raw objects, cleaned output, and reviewed versions remain addressable, so recovery starts at the failing message rather than rerunning the entire document.

documents.title: Chunk Ingestion Tag Gate
documents.summary: Rules first, an LLM only when needed, and one correction gate produce traceable seven-scene tags for every knowledge chunk.

blocks.code:
ruleScenes + confidence → RuleTagQualityGate
├─ confident → correction
└─ weak → LLM whitelist tagging → correction
→ metadata.scenes → embedding

items: The fixed groups are asset, price, volume, trend, valuation, sentiment, and risk_strategy.
Rules bypass the LLM only when at least 2 groups are covered and every hit group reaches the confidence threshold, typically 0.75.
The LLM may select only whitelist tags; correction merges, maps, resolves conflicts, deduplicates, and fills empty groups.
Retrieval reads only final metadata.scenes, never raw ruleScenes or llmScenes.
qualityGate records needLlm, reason, coverage, threshold, and low-confidence groups.
tagVersion and intermediate results enable replay when the taxonomy changes.

documents.title: Instrument Tag Computation Rules
documents.summary: Market, valuation, sentiment-proxy, and risk evidence is normalized to 0..1 and emitted as explainable, asset-aware scene signals.

blocks.code:
continuous  → sigmoid(center, scale)
distribution → percentile_rank(history / industry / asset type)
anomaly     → robust_z_score(median, MAD) → sigmoid
multi-proof → weighted mean or noisy-or

items: Historical percentile outranks fixed thresholds; fallback proceeds through industry and asset-type distributions, then returns missing rather than fake precision.
News and research apply exponential time decay, while labels established by any strong proof can use noisy-or.
Module score uses 0.7 × max(tags) + 0.3 × avg(non-zero tags) so one label cannot fully dominate.
asset, price, volume, trend, valuation, sentiment, and risk_strategy share score, level, direction, tags, evidence, and queryText.
Stock, index, convertible-bond, and fund tags retain asset semantics so similarly named premiums cannot contaminate retrieval.
Price, volume, trend, and most risk rules remain deterministic; policy, news, institutional behavior, and value-trap semantics use model enhancement.

documents.title: Report Generation Pipeline
documents.summary: Retrieval budgets are allocated from current market scenes and evidence is ranked per category instead of using a single global topK.

items: Market state changes the importance of risk, trend, valuation, and other knowledge groups; fixed topK lets high-volume categories crowd out evidence.
The system derives currentScenes and category scores before producing chunkAllocation and grouped retrievalTasks.
The generator receives category-grouped knowledgeContext with source structure preserved.

blocks.code:
POST scene-task → Java task/RMQ → Python currentScenes
→ Java chunkAllocation → Python query embeddings
→ pgvector candidates → Jaccard tags + cross_scene_score → grouped context

items: Java owns task state, allocation policy, and candidate reads; Python owns scene detection and query embeddings.
Vector similarity forms the candidate pool, then tag Jaccard and cross-scene scores calibrate ordering.
The asynchronous boundary makes long reports observable and retryable without pinning one HTTP request.

documents.title: Investor Psychology Scoring
documents.summary: Scenario answers produce six profile dimensions used only to constrain final-answer framing, risk emphasis, and advice strength.

items: Ten scenarios accumulate base scores such as loss anxiety, FOMO, stop-loss discipline, and execution, then aggregate six profile dimensions.
adviceStyle progresses conservatively from risk_first to explicit_trade_light_position; stronger position advice is not exposed in version one.
Chasing, loss aversion, and refusal to stop losses reduce position limits without changing market facts.

blocks.code:
planner → market / knowledge tools → scratchpad
→ load latest profile → final answer constraints → stream

items: The profile is loaded only for final answer generation and never changes what facts the planner should retrieve.
Java owns answers, score aggregation, and the active profile version; Python consumes but does not persist the profile.
Without a profile, the agent falls back to general analysis and risk warnings without personalized sizing.

title: Urban Sidequest
summary: An AI-assisted route decision system for urban exploration.
content: Built on city maps and real POI data, it combines staged candidate retrieval, preference modelling, and route ranking to generate executable, explainable, and adjustable exploration routes.
capabilities: Multi-source POI semantic retrieval and quality filtering
Route preference learning and multi-objective ranking
Explainable route generation with dynamic alternatives

children.name: POI Retrieval
children.detail: Multi-source place retrieval, semantic mapping, and candidate compression

children.name: Route Preference Model
children.detail: Route-quality learning and ranking from preference data

children.name: Route Decision Engine
children.detail: Primary and alternative route generation, explanation, and adjustment

children.name: Android Experience
children.detail: Map selection, route presentation, execution, and check-in feedback

children.name: Backend Services
children.detail: Route orchestration, data services, and a training-data feedback loop

documents.title: Urban Sidequest · Engineering Overview
documents.summary: An explainable city-route system built from POI retrieval, candidate composition, real-segment calibration, and preference learning.

blocks.code:
Compose Map UI → Spring Boot Route Orchestrator
→ POI Retrieval / Ranking → LLM Candidate Composer
→ Amap Calibration → PostGIS / Redis → Explainable A/B/C

items: The POI layer controls eligible places, the route layer controls order and composition, and map services verify reachability.
Rules and models have explicit roles: models do not own geographic facts, and the backend never exposes infeasible drafts.
Selections, dwell, and skip signals become training samples for future preference ranking.
Compose plus StateFlow organizes map state, while Spring Boot currently orchestrates a synchronous route request.
PostGIS handles spatial queries and Redis caches hot candidates and route segments.
The next engineering focus is asynchronous jobs, independent route-quality reranking, and a behavior-driven profile loop.

documents.title: Technical Design Overview
documents.summary: Android owns the interactive map, Spring Boot and PostGIS own reproducible route decisions, and GCJ-02 is used end to end.

items: Android uses Kotlin, Jetpack Compose, Amap Android SDK, and ViewModel plus StateFlow for screen state.
Spring Boot with PostgreSQL/PostGIS, Redis, and Amap Web API owns route rules, caching, audit, and user assets.
Android and Web map keys are separate; inputs, POIs, routes, and rendering remain in GCJ-02.

blocks.code:
validate → POI recall → candidate paths
→ weather/hours/rating/price/risk enrichment
→ rules + time correction → A/B/C routes
→ explanation → audit log

items: The 5,000-user capacity target is protected with rate limits, queues, caches, and explicit dependency-failure states.
The primary API is currently synchronous POST, with an asynchronous, progress-queryable task as the target.
Third-party failures degrade visibly, while location and route data stay isolated by authenticated user.

documents.title: Recommended Route Algorithm
documents.summary: Deterministic rules narrow the POI pool, an LLM composes candidate order, and real map data calibrates and rejects infeasible routes.

blocks.code:
LoadUserPreferenceProfile → semantic mapping → SelectPoiPool
→ BuildCandidateRoutes → CalibrateSegments
→ FilterRoutes → SavePreferenceSamples

items: LinearPoiPoolSelector ranks mustVisit plus linear scores, then PoiDiversitySampler controls category diversity with a maximum pool of 40.
LlmRouteCandidateComposer may arrange only pool IDs into up to 5 drafts and cannot invent POIs, coordinates, distance, time, rating, or hours.
The backend retains hard constraints and acceptance authority; drafts currently keep LLM ordering without a separate quality reranker.
Each adjacent POI pair is calibrated through Amap for actual distance and duration, with caching for repeated segments.
Failures fall back through cache, constrained degradation, and straight-line estimation; invalid segment counts or total time reject the route.
Calibrated route_pref_v5 features are persisted before later execution feedback supplies training labels.

blocks.text: The LLM composes and explains; the backend remains the source of map facts and executability.

documents.path: docs/algorithm/poi/POI线性打分矩阵取值设计.md
documents.title: POI Linear Scoring Matrix
documents.summary: A 36-feature explainable ranker and 8 score rows provide cold-start candidate ranking before diversity sampling.

blocks.code:
X[36] = POI facts + request cross + environment cross + profile cross
S[8] = M(routeGoal, transport, budget, time) × X

items: poi_linear_x_v1 covers short-term interest, semantic role, quality, transport, distance, budget, risk, and profile crosses.
Eight rows emit interest, goal, quality, transport, distance cost, budget cost, risk cost, and personalization.
Linear scoring owns the decision; a neural residual may only compensate at small scale, while must-visit POIs are retained by a hard gate.
Missing ratings, prices, and transit use explicit indicators rather than treating unknown as low quality.
Route goal, transport, budget, and time structure select Delta weights rather than becoming duplicated feature columns.
Training records schema version, names, and values; field ordering changes require a new version.

documents.title: Route X Five-block Features
documents.summary: route_pref_v5 encodes each route as stop, segment, route aggregate, context cross, and candidate-set-relative blocks.

blocks.code:
X = stopMatrix[≤8×38]
  + segmentMatrix[≤7×15]
  + routeDerivedVector[61]
  + contextCrossVector[27]
  + intraSetVector[15]

items: stopMatrix covers POI semantics, quality, price, risk, transit, and role; segmentMatrix covers adjacent movement.
routeDerivedVector aggregates time, flow, diversity, budget, and risk; contextCrossVector expresses user, request, and environment fit.
intraSetVector carries relative rank, deltas, and duplication within one candidate set.
Raw snapshots exist only for audit and rebuild; ranking, acceptance, reason codes, and confidence are supervision Y.
Short matrices are zero-padded and recognized through markers such as isLastStop and segmentEstimateMissing.
Names, order, shape, or missing defaults require a schema bump and historical rebuild; threshold-only edits use thresholdsVersion.

documents.path: docs/algorithm/route/路线偏好排序模型训练设计.md
documents.title: Multi-head Route Preference Model
documents.summary: Five encoders share one representation while learning within-set ranking, absolute recommendation probability, and nine issue labels.

blocks.code:
5 feature encoders → concat(224) → shared encoder
├─ scoreHead → routePreferenceScore
├─ goodnessHead → routeGoodnessLogit
└─ reasonHead MLP → 9 reason logits

items: Stop and segment matrices are padded and flattened first; shared row encoders plus masked pooling remain the small-data fallback.
The current recipe uses hidden_dim 32 and dropout 0.30 after independent LayerNorm and GELU branches.
The reason head gets a private MLP to preserve nonlinear issue subspaces.

blocks.code: total = rankingLoss + 0.30 × goodnessLoss + 0.10 × reasonLoss

items: Weighted pairwise softplus uses pairs only within one candidate set and source weights for real, human, and LLM judgments.
Masked BCE gives goodness an absolute scale and reason a multi-label objective only on rejected routes.
Production goodness uses temperature 1.41 and a default 0.5 threshold; within-set order uses raw preference score.

documents.title: Route Preference Model Runtime
documents.summary: Versioned datasets, artifacts, and prediction outputs keep Python training aligned with the Java route_pref_v5 feature contract.

blocks.code:
MinIO datasets/{version}/
├─ manifest.json
├─ training_samples.parquet   # X
├─ judgments.parquet          # Y
└─ raw_snapshots/             # rebuild / audit

items: X and judgment align by candidate_set_id; pairs and train/valid/test splits stay within or across groups safely.
Training exports weights, feature schema, reason codes, model card, ONNX, and metric plots.
Online writes enter ingest, then an offline builder freezes a new dataset version without reading the product database.
routePreferenceScore ranks within a set without sigmoid; routeGoodnessProb expresses absolute recommendation quality.
reasonCodeScores uses a fixed nine-code vocabulary and rejects unknown values.
Model and feature schema deploy together; new features cannot load an old model silently.

documents.path: docs/algorithm/route/路线裁判与软拒绝设计.md
documents.title: Route Judge and Soft Rejection
documents.summary: Hard execution errors are separated from routes that are feasible but not good enough to recommend.

blocks.code:
LLM routes → Hard Validator
→ Goodness Model + 9 Reason Codes
→ rank / soft reject → retry prompt if needed

items: Hard validation catches missing must-visits, unknown POIs, duplicate stops, overtime, forbidden transport, unreachable segments, and boundary violations.
Goodness estimates user acceptance; pairwise order alone cannot tell whether the first-ranked route is still unacceptable.
Fixed reason codes cover interest, goal, time, fatigue, flow, diversity, repetition, budget, and risk.
When too few routes survive, only primary reason codes and avoidPoiIds enter a retry prompt.
Retry count is capped and never returns an obviously weak route merely to fill three slots.
Judge inference and training share estimated segment features; only selected routes receive full Amap calibration.

documents.path: docs/algorithm/route/LLM模拟用户路线选择设计.md
documents.title: LLM-simulated User Preference
documents.summary: During cold start, multiple simulated judges create auditable ranking and rejection supervision over frozen candidate sets.

items: First-pass judgment reads in-memory generation output without database reads, replanning, or feature recomputation.
One generation is one candidate set; top-up judgment can only revisit the frozen MinIO snapshot.
Candidate X and judgment Y are append-only objects frozen into datasets through a manifest.

blocks.code:
human-readable routes + request + persona → LLM judgment
numeric X / history judgments / behavior labels ✕

items: The prompt sees readable itineraries rather than stopMatrix, segmentMatrix, or training features.
Output is fixed to ranking, accepted/rejected routes, nine reason codes, and confidence; unknown codes fail validation.
Synthetic judgments are marked LLM_SIM_USER and never impersonate clicks, saves, starts, or completions.

documents.title: Simulated Route Judge Pipeline
documents.summary: Persona jobs, Java route generation, multi-model judgments, and MinIO ingestion form a concurrent, top-up capable cold-start data task.

blocks.code:
persona jobs → Java route generation → candidate ingest
→ multi-LLM judge → JSON validation → judgment ingest
→ dataset builder → versioned training set

items: The generator can create 100 personas with 20 requests each across goal, transport, budget, and interest combinations.
A candidate set may receive multi-temperature, multi-model judgments with shuffled display order to reduce position bias.
Route generation and judging use separate pools; retry and fallback failures are discarded instead of becoming corrupted labels.
topup-judgments fills only frozen sets below target-k and never regenerates routes.
Prompt version includes temperature and stores the actual response model for agreement audits.
personalReview exists for human diagnostics only and does not enter Java judgment or labels.

documents.path: docs/user/用户画像问卷与画像表设计.md
documents.title: User Profile and Preference Model
documents.summary: Cold-start answers become fixed preference values, confidence, and extensible tag affinities that are safely shrunk during route requests.

items: user_preference_profiles stores fixed 0..1 dimensions and a global profileConfidence.
user_preference_tag_affinities references a tag catalog, avoiding one database column per evolving interest.
Profile and affinities are upserted or replaced in one transaction, and routing loads data only for the authenticated user.

blocks.code:
effective_preference = base_preference × profileConfidence
profileConfidence = 0  →  personalization = 0

items: Global confidence shrinks low-information cold-start profiles and prevents overconfident recommendations.
Short-term interests supplied for one route and long-term profile affinities remain separate signals.
Version 1 covers questionnaire cold start only; behavior learning and the long-term Android feedback loop remain future work.

title: Scrapider Guidelines
summary: A reusable engineering-guidelines Skill for coding agents.
content: Packages minimal-change discipline, contract preservation, stack-aware reference routing, and verifiable delivery as an installable Skill. It covers Spring Boot, Python, Android Kotlin, and Jetpack Compose, with an independent read-only standards-review agent.
capabilities: Loads engineering guidance according to the active task scope
Enforces minimal changes while preserving established business contracts
Covers Spring Boot, Python, Android Kotlin, and Jetpack Compose

children.name: SKILL.md
children.detail: Defines shared engineering discipline, execution workflow, and stack-aware reference routing

children.name: agents
children.detail: OpenAI configuration and the read-only scrapider-standards-reviewer

children.name: references/java
children.detail: Spring Boot layering, object placement, and Maven multi-module responsibilities

documents.title: Scrapider Engineering Guidelines · README
documents.summary: Composable engineering guidance for Spring Boot, Python, Android Kotlin, and Compose, with references selected by the active stack.

blocks.code:
SKILL.md                # execution entry
agents/                 # standards reviewer
references/java/        # Spring Boot and modules
references/python/      # Python organization
references/android/     # Kotlin / Compose
references/shared/      # cross-stack review

items: The skill identifies the repository stack and existing boundaries before loading only relevant references.
Rules focus on ownership, dependency direction, contracts, and verification rather than forcing one template across ecosystems.
The package supports both implementation guidance and evidence-based standards review.
The target repository AGENTS.md, build constraints, and architectural facts take precedence.
Changes remain local, reuse current capabilities, and finish with risk-proportionate evidence.
Guidance does not replace engineering judgment; justified exceptions state their boundary and reason.

documents.title: Task Execution Protocol
documents.summary: Engineering rules become an executable loop: locate ownership, make the smallest coherent change, and prove contracts remain intact.

blocks.code:
inspect → choose relevant reference → state scope
→ implement surgical change → verify → report evidence

items: State the goal, approach, touched files, and verification path before implementation; load only references relevant to the active stack.
Reuse existing abstractions and avoid one-off layers, wrappers, or duplicate implementations.
Validation belongs at the contract-owning boundary, and changes preserve callers, data models, and error semantics.
Call out changes to public contracts, dependency direction, or data ownership before crossing that boundary.
Do not claim completion without proportionate build, runtime, or source evidence.
Reviews report only actionable issues with file, location, impact, and a scoped correction.

documents.title: Standards Review Agent
documents.summary: The reviewer selects rules from the repository stack and uses source evidence to inspect structure, contracts, concurrency, and maintainability.

items: Read repository and nested rules, build files, and the module graph before selecting Java, Python, Android, or shared guidance.
Trace data from entry points through business ownership, persistence, and external I/O, distinguishing violations from intentional exceptions.
Each finding includes an exact location, reproducible impact, relevant rule, and the smallest suitable correction.

blocks.code:
[severity] concise title
file:line
impact → evidence → recommended boundary

items: Prioritize correctness, contracts, security, resource lifecycle, and dependency direction.
Do not turn personal taste, harmless formatting, or context-free guesses into findings.
When there are no valid findings, state the reviewed scope and residual risk.

documents.title: Spring Boot Backend Boundaries
documents.summary: A clear Controller to Service to Manage to Mapper direction separates transport, orchestration, and persistence.

blocks.code:
Controller → Service → Manage → Mapper → PO
request Param                response VO

items: Controllers own HTTP contracts and parameter entry, never direct Mapper access; Services own use cases and transaction boundaries.
Where a Manage layer exists, it encapsulates aggregate reads and persistence detail instead of duplicating database assembly in Services.
Requests use typed Param models, responses use VOs, and persistence objects do not escape through APIs.
Global advice maps exceptions consistently instead of rebuilding response envelopes in business code.
Handlers or providers are introduced only for a real replaceable protocol, not as empty abstraction.
MQ listeners and publishers each own message contracts, idempotency, and retry semantics.

documents.title: Spring Boot Multi-module Dependencies
documents.summary: Recover real module ownership from POMs and bootstrap wiring, then place runtime behavior along a one-way dependency graph.

items: The bootstrap module owns application startup and configuration assembly, not business implementations.
Business modules own their use cases, runtime behavior, and dependencies on lower-level ports.
Model and persistence modules remain stable boundaries; reverse dependencies must not pull rules into the data layer.

blocks.code:
inspect parent/child POMs → draw dependency direction
→ place change at current owner → verify no cycle

items: Before adding a dependency, check transitive scope and potential cycles.
Cross-module DTOs, events, and interfaces are contracts, so inspect every producer and consumer.
Do not create a shared module for a few reused lines until a stable common meaning is demonstrated.

documents.title: Python Code Organization
documents.summary: Domain logic, workflow orchestration, adapters, and infrastructure keep explicit import direction and replaceable boundaries.

items: Entry points perform configuration, dependency assembly, and lifecycle only; domain functions do not read global environment or implicit singletons.
External APIs, queues, model services, and databases sit behind adapters and enter core logic through typed structures.
Packages expose intentional public APIs and avoid circular imports, cross-layer relative imports, and hidden import side effects.

blocks.code: config → composition root → workflow/service → port → adapter

items: Async boundaries remain consistent, and blocking I/O does not run directly on the event loop.
The composition root owns clients, connections, and worker lifecycle; failures preserve context and the original exception chain.
Configuration is validated at startup rather than scattered environment reads through business code.

documents.title: Android Kotlin and Compose
documents.summary: Unidirectional data flow and stable UI state control recomposition while effects, navigation, and platform resources remain explicit.

blocks.code:
Repository → ViewModel → StateFlow<UiState> → Composable
UI event ────────────────────────────────↑

items: Composables receive immutable state and emit events; network or persistence work does not start in a recomposition path.
ViewModels own screen state and business coroutines; remember or derivedStateOf is used only with a measurable purpose.
Lazy content supplies stable keys, and Modifier order is reviewed across layout, drawing, input, and semantics.
LaunchedEffect, DisposableEffect, and rememberUpdatedState follow lifecycle meaning, with keys matching real dependencies.
Navigation carries minimal stable identifiers and lets the destination ViewModel reload data.
Shared code uses Res.* or platform abstractions instead of depending directly on Android-only APIs.

documents.title: Standards Review
documents.summary: An evidence-driven checklist covers correctness, contracts, boundaries, and verification without reducing review to formatting.

blocks.code:
repository rules → changed behavior → ownership boundary
→ callers/consumers → failure path → verification evidence

items: Identify the behavior to preserve, then inspect callers, structures, errors, and resource lifecycle.
Structural findings explain why ownership is wrong; duplication findings demonstrate stable reusable meaning.
Concurrency, async, and messaging reviews focus on idempotency, cancellation, timeout, retry, and partial failure.
Conclusions must be reproducible from source or runtime evidence and bound their impact accurately.
Recommendations fit the repository architecture instead of substituting a broad refactor for a local defect.
Acceptance targets the closest build, static, runtime, and contract checks for the identified risk.
